package_info.why_malicious: The maintainer introduced code that, after a delay, displays unsolicited political protest messages and opens an external petition site for Russian users. This alters the expected behavior of the package, injects non-technical and disruptive content into production applications, and violates user trust and the principle of least surprise. Such behavior can disrupt application UX, workflows, and may expose users to external advocacy content without consent.

execution_context.trigger: At runtime, 15 seconds after the application loads in a browser environment

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: After 15 seconds of application runtime in the browser, the code displays an alert with a political protest message and opens a Change.org petition in a new browser window or tab, interrupting the user experience.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: The code injects unsolicited, non-functional, and politically motivated content into all applications using the package, regardless of user consent or application context. It leverages browser APIs to display disruptive popups and redirect users to external advocacy sites.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Polyfill packages are expected to provide missing browser features in a transparent manner, without introducing UI popups, alerts, or opening external links unrelated to the technical purpose of the package.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Legitimate use might include user-facing notifications for licensing or critical security issues, but only with explicit user consent and clear documentation. Polyfills should never display arbitrary messages or open external sites.
key_indicators: window.open() to an external petition site (change.org/NetVoyne)
No user opt-in, configuration, or documentation for this behavior
Code executes in all browser contexts regardless of user location or intent

execution_context.trigger: At runtime, when the code is loaded and executed in the browser

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: Constructs a multi-line string containing anti-war and anti-censorship messages, including references to Tor and BBC onion addresses, and a call to action against the Russian government. This string is later used in an alert popup.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: The code injects unsolicited political content into the application context, constructing a message with protest statements and links to external resources. This is unrelated to the package's technical purpose and is delivered to all users indiscriminately.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: A polyfill for the EventSource API should only provide missing browser functionality, not include or display political or protest messages at runtime.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: There is no legitimate reason for a technical library or polyfill to include political statements or advocacy messages in runtime code.
key_indicators: References to external political resources (e.g., Tor, BBC onion addresses)

Presence of setTimeout, alert, and window.open in non-UI utility or polyfill packages
References to external domains (change.org, torproject.org, BBC onion addresses) in source code

detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Scan JavaScript dependencies, especially polyfills and utility libraries, for unexpected use of alert(), window.open(), and setTimeout() with hardcoded delays. Flag any code that constructs or displays unsolicited messages, particularly those containing political content or links to external advocacy sites. Monitor for new or updated versions of widely used packages that introduce such behaviors. Use static analysis to detect hardcoded political messages and references to external domains in source files like eventsource.js.
